The switchgear is configured in a bus A and bus B arrangement, with a main incoming circuit breaker for each bus section and an interconnecting bus tie circuit breaker between the two bus sections. This configuration will allow the facility to continue operation at reduced capacity should one section of the switchgear or one of the upstream transformers be out of service. The 13.8 kV switchgear will supply power directly to high voltage and downstream low voltage (LV) consumers, including: Page62 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version  CO Compressors 2  CO Offloading Pumps 2  Vaporizer Heater  480 V power distribution (transformers and switchboards) for low voltage process and utilities consumers 4.4.3 LOW VOLTAGE POWER DISTRIBUTION The low voltage 480 V switchgear is configured in a bus A and bus B arrangement, with a main incoming circuit breaker for each bus section and an interconnecting bus tie circuit breaker between the two bus sections. Each main circuit breaker receives power from a dedicated upstream 13.8/0.48 kV power distribution transformer. The low voltage switchgear and associated power transformers located in the electrical room of the main site building. The power distribution transformers supplying the 480 V switchgear are rated to supply power to both bus to allow the facility to continue operation should the alternate transformer be out of service. The neutral point of the transformer secondary windings will be resistance grounded through a neutral grounding resistor that is rated to limit fault current to 100 Amps during a ground fault event. The transformers are intended to be dry-type, with natural and forced air cooling to achieve the required power rating. The 480 V switchgear will supply power directly to 480 V consumers, primarily motor driven loads, and supply power to two main 208/120 V small power distribution panel boards via small power distribution transformers. The main small power distribution boards will in turn supply small power consumers throughout the facility. The neutral point of the transformer secondary windings will be solidly grounded, with no neutral grounding resistor used. This small power design will be further evaluated in the next study phase to determine if remotely located sub-distribution panel boards outside the main electrical room will allow the small power design to be optimized (e.g., reduced power lengths) or whether the current design of centrally located panels only is preferred.
